_about: Physical limits the claims check (engine/claims_check.py) applies in code, per kind of product. They are generous on purpose: a claim is called not_possible only when it breaks the limit of the best technology there is, and doubtful when it breaks what is normal on the market. Add a kind of product by adding a block here and a rule in engine/claims_check.py.

power_bank._why_volts: Power-bank mAh is quoted at the lithium cell's 3.7 V, so energy (Wh) = mAh x 3.7 / 1000.
power_bank._why_impossible: Best lithium-ion cells today hold about 250-270 Wh per kg, before the casing and circuit. Under this weight the cells alone cannot fit.
power_bank._why_doubtful: A finished power bank (cells, case, circuit) rarely reaches 200 Wh per kg.

charger._why: The smallest GaN chargers on sale carry about 1 W per gram. Twice that is beyond current technology; over 1.2 W per gram is unusual.
charger._why_usb_pd: USB Power Delivery 3.1 (the USB-C standard) tops out at 240 W, so a USB-C charger or cable cannot claim more.

energy_saver._why: A plug-in box cannot cut a home's bill: home meters bill the energy a device actually uses (kWh), and these boxes only change the power factor, which household meters do not bill. A product that really uses less energy (an LED bulb, an inverter AC) says what it does.
